title: 30% minimum tax on discretionary (family) trusts
headline: Proposed: family trust trustees pay at least 30% on trust income from 2028-29, credited to individual beneficiaries but not refunded. Not law yet.
summary: The trustee of a discretionary trust would pay a minimum 30% tax on the trust's income. Individual beneficiaries get a non-refundable offset for it, so beneficiaries on rates below 30% effectively pay 30%. The bills passed the House on 29 October 2026 and are before the Senate.

history.note: Tax Reform No. 3 Bill and the minimum tax imposition bill
Third reading 91 to 45; Senate committee recommended passage on 13 November

bigStat.caption: minimum tax on discretionary trust income

before: Trust income flows through and is taxed at each beneficiary's marginal rate, so income can be directed to family members on low rates.
after: If passed, the trustee pays at least 30% on the trust's minimum tax income from 2028-29.
Individual beneficiaries get a non-refundable offset for that tax. Company beneficiaries and exempt entities get no offset.
The trustee uses franking credits against the minimum tax; any excess is refunded to the trustee.
A roll-over from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2030 lets trusts restructure into a company or fixed trust without income tax; stamp duty and GST can still apply.
exemptions: Fixed trusts, widely held trusts, managed investment trusts and CCIVs.
Special disability trusts, deceased estates, qualifying testamentary trust income and complying super funds.
Primary production income, and charitable or other exempt-entity trusts.

workedExample.title: Explanatory Memorandum example 1.1
steps: A trust has net income of $200,000 and distributes it all to individual beneficiaries.
The trustee pays the minimum tax: $200,000 × 30% = $60,000.
Each beneficiary is taxed on their share as usual and claims an offset of 30% of it.
workedExample.result: The $60,000 counts towards the beneficiaries' own tax, but the offset can't be refunded, so a beneficiary on a rate below 30% effectively pays 30%.

actions.text: Check whether your trust would be a 'minimum tax trust' or falls into one of the exclusions.
Note the decision windows: restructure roll-over from 1 July 2027 to 30 June 2030, or a one-off election in 2028-29. A trust can't use both.
Get state stamp duty advice before any restructure: the roll-over covers income tax only.
Watch the Senate vote, expected in the 23 to 26 November 2026 sitting week, and any amendments.

positions.summary: Introduced the bills and says it has not changed its position on the exemptions.
Opposes the trust tax and wants an inquiry, or at least a start no earlier than 1 July 2029. Its leadership has committed to repeal.
Will pass the bills once the exemption for income sent to unauthorised charities and tax-exempt entities is removed. Also wants a beneficial ownership register that covers trusts.
Opposed the trust tax after the Budget; its House MPs voted against the bill.

caveats: Some trade press reported a 1 July 2027 start. Parliament's documents and the ATO say 1 July 2028; 1 July 2027 is when the restructure window opens.
Collection, PAYG instalment and reporting rules are still to come in later laws.
The bill may be amended in the Senate, for example on distributions to charities.
